entities.name: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Clear cell kidney → VHL and chromosome 3p.
snv: Driver — VHL inactivation
Cooperating — PBRM1, SETD2, BAP1, MTOR
other: Alternative VHL inactivation — promoter methylation
entities.pitfall: Alterations are subset-dependent and require histologic context; none should be assumed present in every case.

entities.name: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Papillary kidney → MET in a subset; gains of 7 and 17.
snv: Driver — MET activation (subset)
cnv: Characteristic — gains of chromosomes 7 and 17; Y loss in subsets
entities.pitfall: Former type 1/type 2 subdivision is not used here. Several former type 2 tumors now belong to molecularly defined entities.

entities.name: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Chromophobe → multiple chromosome losses.
snv: Cooperating — TP53, PTEN (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Not every tumor loses every chromosome; this is a recurring dosage pattern.

entities.name: TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: TFE3 kidney cancer → fusion-driven transcription.
rearr: Defining — TFE3 fusions, including ASPSCR1::TFE3, PRCC::TFE3, SFPQ::TFE3
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: TFEB-altered renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: TFEB can be rearranged or amplified.
rearr: Defining subset — MALAT1::TFEB and alternative partners
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: FH-deficient renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: FH loss → fumarate accumulation.
snv: Defining — biallelic FH inactivation
cnv: Driver — FH deletion as one possible second hit
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: SDH-deficient renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: SDH-complex loss → succinate accumulation.
snv: Defining — SDHB, SDHC, SDHD or SDHA inactivation
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: ELOC-mutated renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: ELOC belongs to the VHL complex.
snv: Defining — ELOC (TCEB1) mutation
cnv: Cooperating — chromosome 8 loss affecting the second ELOC allele
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: A kidney carcinoma can be ALK-fusion driven.
rearr: Defining — ALK fusions, including VCL::ALK, TPM3::ALK, STRN::ALK
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma
entities.anchor: Medullary kidney + SMARCB1 loss.
snv: Defining mechanism — SMARCB1 inactivation
rearr: Driver — disruptive SMARCB1 rearrangements
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: Eosinophilic solid and cystic renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: ESC kidney cancer → TSC1/TSC2–mTOR.
snv: Driver — TSC1 or TSC2 inactivation
entities.pitfall: Molecularly distinct renal entity; germline predisposition and tumor-only alterations must be distinguished where relevant.

entities.name: Collecting duct carcinoma
entities.anchor: Collecting duct carcinoma lacks one obligate driver.
snv: Recurrent — NF2, SETD2, CDKN2A and SMARCB1 alterations (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Exclude renal medullary, FH-deficient and urothelial carcinomas before assigning this rare diagnosis.

entities.name: Mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Mucinous tubular/spindle kidney → chromosome losses.
cnv: Characteristic — multiple whole-chromosome losses, including 1, 4, 6, 8, 9, 13, 14 and 15
entities.pitfall: No universal point mutation or fusion is established; avoid confusing it with papillary RCC.

entities.name: Tubulocystic renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Tubulocystic morphology has no single defining driver.
entities.pitfall: Poorly differentiated components warrant exclusion of FH-deficient RCC. No reliable universal driver is summarized.

entities.name: Acquired cystic disease-associated renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Dialysis-associated cystic kidney context matters.
cnv: Recurrent — chromosome gains, variable across tumors
entities.pitfall: No single defining recurrent SNV/fusion established; distinguish from other RCC in acquired cystic kidneys.

entities.name: Renal cell carcinoma, NOS
entities.anchor: Unclassified kidney carcinoma has heterogeneous genetics.
entities.pitfall: An exclusion category after recognized morphologic and molecular entities have been evaluated.

entities.name: Wilms tumor
entities.anchor: Wilms → WT1/WNT, imprinting and microRNA processing.
snv: Drivers — WT1, CTNNB1, AMER1; DROSHA, DGCR8, SIX1/2 subsets
Progression — TP53 in anaplastic tumors
other: Driver context — 11p15 imprinting abnormalities / IGF2 dysregulation
entities.pitfall: Most cases are not explained by WT1 alone; tumor predisposition mechanisms can be germline or epigenetic.

entities.name: Clear cell sarcoma of kidney
entities.anchor: CCSK → BCOR internal tandem duplication.
snv: Driver — BCOR exon 15 internal tandem duplication
rearr: Alternative — YWHAE::NUTM2; rare BCOR fusions
entities.pitfall: Distinct from clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue and clear cell RCC. BCOR ITD is not a copy-number amplification.

entities.name: Rhabdoid tumor of kidney
entities.anchor: Renal rhabdoid → SMARCB1 loss.
snv: Driver — SMARCB1 inactivation
entities.pitfall: Germline SMARCB1 predisposition is possible. Same core pathway as extrarenal rhabdoid tumors.

entities.name: Urothelial carcinoma
entities.anchor: Urothelial → FGFR3/TERT or TP53/RB1 routes.
snv: Drivers — TERT promoter, FGFR3, PIK3CA; TP53, RB1, KDM6A, ARID1A, STAG2 (variable)
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A loss; ERBB2, CCND1, E2F3 amplifications
rearr: Subset — FGFR3::TACC3 and alternative FGFR3 fusions
entities.pitfall: Bladder, renal pelvis, ureter and urethral sites grouped. Noninvasive papillary carcinoma included; carcinoma in situ is excluded as a separate entry.

entities.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of urinary tract
entities.anchor: Urinary squamous carcinoma → heterogeneous TP53/cell-cycle lesions.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, CDKN2A and PI3K-pathway alterations
entities.pitfall: Pure squamous carcinoma differs from urothelial carcinoma with squamous differentiation; no defining single driver.

entities.name: Adenocarcinoma of urinary tract
entities.anchor: Urinary adenocarcinoma often uses RAS/PI3K and TP53 pathways.
snv: Recurrent — KRAS, TP53, PIK3CA (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Bladder/urethral glandular carcinomas are heterogeneous. Exclude a colorectal or other metastasis.

entities.name: Urachal carcinoma
entities.anchor: Urachal adenocarcinoma: KRAS/TP53 in subsets.
snv: Recurrent — KRAS, TP53; less often BRAF or PIK3CA
entities.pitfall: Enteric morphology and some mutations overlap colorectal cancer; anatomical origin is critical.

entities.name: Clear cell adenocarcinoma of urinary tract
entities.anchor: Urinary clear cell carcinoma is not clear cell RCC.
snv: Reported — PIK3CA, KRAS, ARID1A and other alterations (small series)
entities.pitfall: Rare Müllerian-type tumor; no single established defining molecular hallmark.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of urinary tract
entities.anchor: Urinary NEC → TP53/RB1 loss.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, RB1; TERT promoter in many bladder cases
entities.pitfall: Small- and large-cell forms combined; genomic overlap with urothelial carcinoma can reflect a shared clone.

entities.name: Prostate adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Prostate → ETS fusion or SPOP; PTEN is a frequent partner.
snv: Drivers/subsets — SPOP, FOXA1, IDH1
Cooperating — TP53; DNA-repair genes BRCA2, ATM, CDK12
cnv: Progression — AR amplification in treated advanced disease
rearr: Drivers — TMPRSS2::ERG and other ETS-family rearrangements
entities.pitfall: Acinar and ductal forms combined. AR amplification often reflects treatment-selected progression rather than initial tumor formation.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of prostate
entities.anchor: Prostatic NEC → combined RB1 and TP53 disruption.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, RB1
cnv: Cooperating — RB1 loss; MYCN/AURKA amplification in subsets
rearr: Shared-origin marker — TMPRSS2::ERG in some cases
entities.pitfall: Includes de novo and treatment-related disease; AR-independent lineage evolution differs from usual adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Basal cell carcinoma of prostate
entities.anchor: Prostatic basal cell carcinoma can show MYB-family biology.
rearr: Subset — MYB::NFIB
entities.pitfall: Rare, not equivalent to cutaneous basal cell carcinoma; PTCH1/SMO should not be assumed.

entities.name: Squamous / adenosquamous carcinoma of prostate
entities.anchor: Rare prostatic squamous malignancy has no uniform driver.
snv: Reported — TP53 and other carcinoma-associated alterations
entities.pitfall: Exclude secondary involvement; some cases arise after treatment of prostatic adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Carcinoma of seminal vesicle
entities.anchor: A rare site with no validated defining driver.
entities.pitfall: Adenocarcinoma and very rare squamous carcinoma grouped; exclude direct extension from prostate or bladder.

entities.name: Carcinoma of rete testis / epididymis
entities.anchor: Adnexal testicular carcinomas are molecularly undercharacterized.
entities.pitfall: Adenocarcinoma and rare squamous/ovarian-type carcinomas grouped. No recurrent driver should be assumed from morphology alone.

entities.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of penis / scrotum
entities.anchor: HPV-driven or TP53/cell-cycle driven.
snv: HPV-independent subsets — TP53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, PIK3CA
other: Viral — high-risk HPV in the associated group
entities.pitfall: HPV-driven p53/RB dysfunction need not involve TP53/RB1 gene mutations.

entities.name: Leydig cell tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Malignant Leydig tumor lacks a universal driver.
snv: Reported — TP53, FH and other alterations in subsets
entities.pitfall: Only malignant disease is included; findings in benign Leydig tumors should not be generalized to every malignant case.

entities.name: Sertoli cell tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Sertoli biology: WNT or PRKAR1A in selected forms.
snv: Subset — CTNNB1 activation; PRKAR1A inactivation in large-cell calcifying tumors
entities.pitfall: Most Sertoli tumors are benign. These alterations establish a pathway, not malignant behavior.

entities.name: Other malignant testicular sex cord–stromal tumors
entities.anchor: Rare malignant stromal groups have limited driver data.
entities.pitfall: Granulosa-cell, mixed and NOS malignant testicular stromal tumors included; ovarian FOXL2 frequency should not be transplanted to testicular disease.

entities.name: Germinoma family (seminoma / dysgerminoma / germinoma)
entities.anchor: Germinoma family → KIT/RAS; dosage differs by site.
snv: Driver — KIT; KRAS/NRAS (subsets)
cnv: Characteristic — 12p gain/i(12p) in postpubertal testicular GCT; not universal across ovarian/CNS sites
entities.pitfall: One broad lineage entry with testis, ovary, CNS and extragonadal aliases. Site-specific prevalence differs.

entities.name: Embryonal carcinoma
entities.anchor: Embryonal carcinoma: aneuploidy more than a recurrent hotspot.
cnv: Characteristic in postpubertal testicular disease — 12p gain/i(12p)
entities.pitfall: Primarily postpubertal GCT; no single obligatory SNV/fusion.

entities.name: Yolk sac tumor
entities.anchor: Yolk sac tumor: developmental lineage, variable chromosome changes.
cnv: Characteristic in postpubertal testicular disease — 12p gain/i(12p)
entities.pitfall: Prepubertal and ovarian tumors need not have the postpubertal testicular 12p signature.

entities.name: Choriocarcinoma, nongestational
entities.anchor: Nongestational choriocarcinoma belongs to the GCT spectrum.
cnv: Characteristic in postpubertal testicular disease — 12p gain/i(12p)
entities.pitfall: Gestational choriocarcinoma is separately listed under female genital tumors.

entities.name: Teratoma, malignant-context germ-cell tumor
entities.anchor: Postpubertal testicular teratoma shares GCT 12p biology.
cnv: Characteristic in postpubertal testicular disease — 12p gain/i(12p)
entities.pitfall: Includes postpubertal testicular teratoma and ovarian immature teratoma. Mature ovarian and prepubertal teratomas are excluded; ovarian immature tumors have distinct genomic patterns.

entities.name: Mixed germ-cell tumor
entities.anchor: A mixed tumor shares its germ-cell lineage genome.
cnv: Characteristic in postpubertal testicular disease — 12p gain/i(12p)
entities.pitfall: Molecular findings vary with age, site and components.

entities.name: Teratoma with somatic-type malignancy
entities.anchor: GCT origin can persist beneath somatic cancer morphology.
cnv: Characteristic in postpubertal testicular disease — 12p gain/i(12p)
entities.pitfall: Somatic components acquire lineage-specific drivers. Establish origin rather than assume every somatic tumor near a teratoma is related.

entities.name: Spermatocytic tumor
entities.anchor: Spermatocytic tumor differs from seminoma.
snv: Subset — FGFR3 or HRAS activating variants
entities.pitfall: Usually indolent but classified separately; sarcomatous transformation can confer aggressive behavior. Not the usual 12p/GCNIS pathway.

entities.name: High-grade serous carcinoma, tubo-ovarian / peritoneal
entities.anchor: High-grade serous → TP53 plus HR-repair or CCNE1 routes.
snv: Driver — TP53
Subset — BRCA1/2 and other homologous-recombination repair defects
other: Alternative repair defect — BRCA1 promoter methylation
entities.pitfall: Somatic and germline BRCA alterations are distinct. Fallopian-tube, ovarian and primary-peritoneal presentations combined.

entities.name: Low-grade serous carcinoma
entities.anchor: Low-grade serous → MAPK, not the usual TP53 route.
snv: Driver — KRAS, BRAF, NRAS (alternative subsets)
entities.pitfall: Separate disease from high-grade serous carcinoma; serous borderline tumors are excluded.

entities.name: Endometrioid carcinoma of ovary
entities.anchor: Ovarian endometrioid → WNT/PI3K and chromatin.
snv: Drivers — CTNNB1, PTEN, PIK3CA, ARID1A; TP53 in a subset
other: Subset — mismatch-repair deficiency
entities.pitfall: May arise in endometriosis; assess distinction from uterine primary or metastasis.

entities.name: Clear cell carcinoma of ovary
entities.anchor: Ovarian clear cell → ARID1A + PIK3CA.
snv: Driver/cooperating — ARID1A loss, PIK3CA activation
entities.pitfall: Endometriosis-associated; the genotype does not resemble VHL-driven clear cell kidney cancer.

entities.name: Mucinous carcinoma of ovary
entities.anchor: Ovarian mucinous → KRAS, CDKN2A, TP53 ± ERBB2.
snv: Drivers/cooperating — KRAS, TP53, CDKN2A; RNF43 (subset)
entities.pitfall: Exclude metastatic GI/pancreatobiliary mucinous tumors; shared mutations do not prove ovarian origin.

entities.name: Brenner tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Malignant Brenner: cell-cycle/PI3K alterations in small series.
snv: Reported — PIK3CA, TP53 and CDKN2A alterations
entities.pitfall: Evidence is limited; exclude metastatic urothelial carcinoma and benign/borderline Brenner tumor.

entities.name: Carcinosarcoma of female genital tract
entities.anchor: Carcinosarcoma: carcinoma with sarcomatous differentiation.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, PIK3CA, PTEN, PPP2R1A, FBXW7
cnv: Subset — ERBB2 amplification; extensive chromosome changes
entities.pitfall: Uterine, ovarian and rare lower-tract sites grouped; no obligatory fusion. The two components often share a clone.

entities.name: Small cell carcinoma of ovary, hypercalcemic type
entities.anchor: SCCOHT → SMARCA4 loss.
snv: Defining driver — SMARCA4 inactivation
entities.pitfall: Not ordinary pulmonary-type neuroendocrine small cell carcinoma. Germline predisposition occurs.

entities.name: Adult granulosa cell tumor of ovary
entities.anchor: Adult granulosa → FOXL2 C134W.
snv: Characteristic driver — FOXL2 p.C134W
entities.pitfall: Highly characteristic but interpret in context; does not imply the juvenile form has the same mutation.

entities.name: Juvenile granulosa cell tumor of ovary
entities.anchor: Juvenile granulosa → variable AKT/G-protein signaling.
snv: Subset — AKT1 internal tandem duplications; GNAS activating variants
entities.pitfall: FOXL2 C134W is usually absent; age alone does not classify adult versus juvenile tumor.

entities.name: Sertoli–Leydig cell tumor of ovary
entities.anchor: Sertoli–Leydig → DICER1 RNase IIIb.
snv: Driver — DICER1 RNase IIIb hotspot with a second loss-of-function hit (subset)
entities.pitfall: DICER1 is enriched in moderately/poorly differentiated tumors; may include a germline hit. Well-differentiated benign tumors are outside scope.

entities.name: Other malignant ovarian sex cord–stromal tumors
entities.anchor: Rare ovarian stromal malignancies lack a universal signature.
snv: Subtype association — STK11 in Peutz–Jeghers-associated sex cord tumor with annular tubules
entities.pitfall: Study umbrella for malignant steroid/Sertoli/annular-tubule, mixed and NOS tumors. Most related benign entities are excluded.

entities.name: Ovarian fibrosarcoma
entities.anchor: Ovarian fibrosarcoma: complex, nonspecific genetics.
entities.pitfall: No established recurrent defining driver; distinguish from mitotically active cellular fibroma.

entities.name: Endometrioid carcinoma of endometrium
entities.anchor: Endometrioid uterus → PTEN/PI3K, WNT and molecular classes.
snv: Drivers — PTEN, PIK3CA, PIK3R1, CTNNB1, ARID1A, KRAS
Subset-defining molecular group — pathogenic POLE exonuclease-domain variants
Subset — mismatch-repair gene inactivation or TP53 alterations
other: Common MMR-deficiency mechanism — MLH1 promoter methylation
entities.pitfall: POLE-mutant, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal and no-specific-molecular-profile groups cut across histology; not all POLE variants are pathogenic.

entities.name: Serous carcinoma of endometrium
entities.anchor: Uterine serous → TP53 and copy-number changes.
snv: Driver — TP53; PIK3CA, PPP2R1A, FBXW7 (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Do not assume the BRCA/HR-deficient profile of tubo-ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma.

entities.name: Clear cell carcinoma of endometrium
entities.anchor: Endometrial clear cell has heterogeneous PI3K/chromatin biology.
snv: Recurrent — PIK3CA, ARID1A, PTEN, TP53 (subsets)
entities.pitfall: No single defining mutation; molecular classes can overlap with other endometrial carcinomas.

entities.name: Undifferentiated / dedifferentiated endometrial carcinoma
entities.anchor: Dedifferentiation can follow SWI/SNF loss.
snv: Subset — SMARCA4, SMARCB1, ARID1A/ARID1B inactivation
other: Subset — mismatch-repair deficiency
entities.pitfall: SWI/SNF loss occurs in only a subset and must be interpreted with epithelial differentiation.

entities.name: Mesonephric / mesonephric-like adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Mesonephric lineage → KRAS and 1q gain.
snv: Driver — KRAS; NRAS in a smaller subset
entities.pitfall: Cervical mesonephric and uterine/ovarian mesonephric-like tumors grouped for study, with distinct anatomical origins.

entities.name: Adenocarcinoma of cervix
entities.anchor: Cervical adenocarcinoma: HPV-associated and independent routes.
snv: Subset — PIK3CA, KRAS, ERBB2
Gastric-type subset — TP53, STK11, KRAS
other: Viral — high-risk HPV in usual-type/associated tumors; absent in gastric-type, mesonephric and clear-cell groups
entities.pitfall: Broad entry keeps HPV-independent gastric and clear-cell variants explicit. Mesonephric biology is separately cross-referenced.

entities.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of cervix
entities.anchor: Cervical SCC → HPV, with PI3K-pathway cooperation.
snv: Cooperating — PIK3CA; PTEN, FBXW7 and others (subsets)
other: Etiologic — high-risk HPV in the great majority
entities.pitfall: HPV-independent cases exist. Viral p53/RB inhibition is not the same as TP53/RB1 mutation.

entities.name: Adenosquamous carcinoma of cervix
entities.anchor: Cervical adenosquamous usually shares HPV-driven biology.
snv: Recurrent — PIK3CA and other cervical-carcinoma pathway changes
other: Viral — high-risk HPV in most cases
entities.pitfall: No specific recurrent fusion defines the mixed squamous/glandular phenotype.

entities.name: Adenoid basal carcinoma of cervix
entities.anchor: Adenoid basal carcinoma is often HPV-associated.
other: Viral — high-risk HPV association
entities.pitfall: Rare, often indolent; distinguish from adenoid cystic carcinoma and associated invasive squamous carcinoma.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of female genital tract
aliases: ovarian pulmonary type small cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: High-grade NEC: HPV at cervix, variable TP53/RB elsewhere.
snv: Recurrent — TP53/RB1 and PI3K/RAS-pathway alterations, site-dependent
other: Viral — high-risk HPV in most cervical cases
entities.pitfall: Small- and large-cell NEC grouped; ovarian hypercalcemic-type small cell carcinoma is a separate SMARCA4-driven entity.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine tumor of female genital tract
entities.anchor: Well-differentiated genital NETs have limited recurrent-driver data.
entities.pitfall: Includes ovarian carcinoid and very rare uterine/cervical NETs; exclude metastatic digestive or lung NET.

entities.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of vulva
entities.anchor: Vulvar SCC: HPV pathway or TP53 pathway.
snv: HPV-independent subsets — TP53; HRAS, PIK3CA and NOTCH-pathway alterations
other: Viral — high-risk HPV in the associated group
entities.pitfall: HPV-independent/p53-wildtype tumors also occur; this is not a strict two-gene dichotomy.

entities.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of vagina
entities.anchor: Vaginal SCC is often HPV-associated.
snv: Cooperating — PI3K-pathway alterations; TP53 in independent subsets
other: Viral — high-risk HPV in many cases
entities.pitfall: Exclude extension from cervix or vulva; site is part of classification.

entities.name: Adenocarcinoma of vagina
entities.anchor: Vaginal glandular cancers are a diverse rare family.
snv: Reported — PIK3CA, KRAS, TP53 depending on histology
other: Context — HPV-associated subset; DES exposure in a subset of clear-cell tumors
entities.pitfall: Clear-cell, endometrioid, gastric, intestinal and rare Skene-type variants grouped. Mesonephric carcinoma is cross-referenced separately.

entities.name: Adenocarcinoma of vulva / Bartholin gland
entities.anchor: Glandular subtype determines the molecular clue.
snv: Subset — PIK3CA, TP53 and other glandular-carcinoma lesions
rearr: Adenoid cystic subset — MYB-family rearrangement
entities.pitfall: Bartholin, mammary-type, intestinal and sweat-gland-type carcinomas grouped; refer to matching salivary/skin analogues, with site-specific caution.

entities.name: Endometrial stromal sarcoma
entities.anchor: Low grade: JAZF1; high grade: YWHAE or BCOR.
snv: High-grade subset — BCOR internal tandem duplication
rearr: Low-grade subset — JAZF1::SUZ12; PHF1-related fusions
High-grade subset — YWHAE::NUTM2A/B; ZC3H7B::BCOR
entities.pitfall: Low- and high-grade categories combined only for the study layout. They are distinct WHO diseases with different fusion biology.

entities.name: Müllerian adenosarcoma
entities.anchor: Adenosarcoma: malignant stroma with heterogeneous drivers.
snv: Recurrent — DICER1 (subset); TP53 in aggressive tumors
entities.pitfall: Uterine, cervical, ovarian and vaginal sites grouped; no obligatory defining fusion.

entities.name: Undifferentiated uterine sarcoma
entities.anchor: An exclusion diagnosis after fusion-defined sarcomas.
snv: Recurrent — TP53 and other tumor-suppressor lesions (variable)
entities.pitfall: Exclude high-grade ESS, leiomyosarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma and molecularly defined sarcomas.

entities.name: Uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: UTROSCT → NCOA-family fusions.
rearr: Characteristic — ESR1::NCOA3; GREB1::NCOA1/2 and related fusions
entities.pitfall: Only malignant/metastasizing cases within scope; a fusion does not itself prove malignant behavior.

entities.name: SMARCA4-deficient uterine sarcoma
entities.anchor: Undifferentiated uterine sarcoma + SMARCA4 loss.
snv: Driver — SMARCA4 inactivation
entities.pitfall: An emerging molecularly defined sarcoma; distinguish from dedifferentiated endometrial carcinoma.

entities.name: Gestational choriocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Gestational origin is shown by parental-genome analysis.
other: Defining context — conceptus-derived trophoblast, often demonstrable paternal alleles
entities.pitfall: No universal recurrent somatic driver. Genotyping distinguishes gestational from nongestational disease; paternal DNA is not an oncogenic gene fusion.

entities.name: Placental site trophoblastic tumor
entities.anchor: PSTT: implantation-site trophoblast, no universal genetic driver.
other: Defining context — gestational/conceptus-derived genome
entities.pitfall: Specific recurrent initiating SNV/CNV/fusion not established; rare nongestational trophoblastic tumors need separate context.

entities.name: Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor
entities.anchor: ETT: chorionic-type intermediate trophoblast.
other: Defining context — gestational/conceptus-derived genome in typical cases
entities.pitfall: No universal recurrent driver; morphology and genotyping differ from squamous carcinoma.

entities.name: Invasive hydatidiform mole
entities.anchor: An invasive mole is a gestational genomic disorder.
other: Typical complete-mole background — androgenetic diploidy
Partial-mole background — usually diandric triploidy
entities.pitfall: Included as invasive gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Noninvasive moles are excluded; ploidy is not a focal CNV driver.

entities.name: Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Squamous head/neck: TP53–cell cycle or viral oncogenesis.
snv: HPV-independent drivers — TP53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1; PIK3CA/HRAS subsets
other: Viral — high-risk HPV is especially important in oropharyngeal disease
entities.pitfall: Site-specific HPV interpretation is essential; p16 is not a universal surrogate at all head/neck sites. Histologic variants combined.

entities.name: Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Squamous head/neck: TP53–cell cycle or viral oncogenesis.
snv: HPV-independent drivers — TP53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1; PIK3CA/HRAS subsets
other: Viral — high-risk HPV is especially important in oropharyngeal disease
entities.pitfall: Site-specific HPV interpretation is essential; p16 is not a universal surrogate at all head/neck sites. Histologic variants combined.

entities.name: Laryngeal / hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Squamous head/neck: TP53–cell cycle or viral oncogenesis.
snv: HPV-independent drivers — TP53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1; PIK3CA/HRAS subsets
other: Viral — high-risk HPV is especially important in oropharyngeal disease
entities.pitfall: Site-specific HPV interpretation is essential; p16 is not a universal surrogate at all head/neck sites. Histologic variants combined.

entities.name: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma
entities.anchor: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma often uses EBV and NF-κB.
snv: Cooperating — NF-κB pathway lesions; TP53 in subsets
other: Etiologic — EBV in most nonkeratinizing tumors
entities.pitfall: Keratinizing and nonkeratinizing forms grouped; viral status varies with histologic and geographical context.

entities.name: Low-grade nasopharyngeal papillary adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Rare papillary nasopharyngeal carcinoma: no established driver.
entities.pitfall: Thyroid-like morphology does not establish thyroid origin or a thyroid-type BRAF/RET genotype.

entities.name: Sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Sinonasal SCC: HPV or papilloma-related EGFR routes in subsets.
snv: Subset — EGFR exon 20 insertions, especially inverted-papilloma-associated disease
Cooperating — TP53, CDKN2A, PIK3CA
other: Viral — high-risk HPV in a subset
entities.pitfall: Keratinizing/nonkeratinizing histology grouped; exclude NUT and SWI/SNF-deficient carcinomas.

entities.name: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
entities.anchor: SNUC → IDH2 R172 in a substantial subset.
snv: Driver — IDH2 R172 (subset)
Cooperating — TP53, PI3K-pathway and chromatin lesions
entities.pitfall: Exclude separately defined NUT and SWI/SNF-deficient tumors; old SNUC cohorts mixed several molecular diseases.

entities.name: SWI/SNF-deficient sinonasal carcinoma
entities.anchor: Sinonasal carcinoma can lose SMARCB1 or SMARCA4.
snv: Defining mechanism — SMARCB1 or SMARCA4 inactivation
entities.pitfall: Two distinct protein-deficient groups nested in one study entry; immunostain loss does not specify the exact DNA lesion.

entities.name: NUT carcinoma
entities.anchor: NUT carcinoma → NUTM1 rearrangement.
rearr: Defining — BRD4::NUTM1; BRD3::NUTM1, NSD3::NUTM1 and alternative partners
entities.pitfall: Can arise in thorax or head/neck; NUTM1 fusions also occur in other lineages, so fusion partner and morphology matter.

entities.name: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma
entities.anchor: A salivary-like sinonasal cancer driven by HPV.
other: Defining viral association — high-risk HPV, frequently type 33
entities.pitfall: An adenoid-cystic-like appearance does not mean MYB/MYBL1 fusion; classic adenoid cystic carcinoma is distinct.

entities.name: Intestinal-type sinonasal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Sinonasal intestinal-type: TP53 and RAS/WNT subsets.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, KRAS, APC/CTNNB1 alterations (variable)
entities.pitfall: Exclude metastatic colorectal carcinoma; molecular resemblance is not proof of a common origin.

entities.name: Nonintestinal-type sinonasal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Nonintestinal sinonasal adenocarcinoma is heterogeneous.
rearr: Reported low-grade subset — ETV6-related fusions, including ETV6::NTRK3
entities.pitfall: No uniform driver; salivary-type entities and metastases must be excluded.

entities.name: Olfactory neuroblastoma
entities.anchor: Olfactory neuroblastoma has no single defining genetic driver.
snv: Subset — TP53 and chromatin/PI3K-pathway alterations
entities.pitfall: Not the same molecular disease as peripheral neuroblastoma; MYCN amplification is not a universal ONB hallmark.

entities.name: Biphenotypic sinonasal sarcoma
entities.anchor: Biphenotypic sinonasal sarcoma → PAX3 fusion.
rearr: Characteristic — PAX3::MAML3; alternative PAX3 partners
entities.pitfall: The fusion partner matters: PAX3::FOXO1 also occurs in rhabdomyosarcoma.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of head and neck
entities.anchor: Head/neck high-grade NEC: TP53/RB pathway in subsets.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, RB1; site-dependent PI3K/RAS-pathway alterations
entities.pitfall: Small- and large-cell forms grouped. Exclude olfactory neuroblastoma and IDH2/SWI-SNF-defined sinonasal tumors.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine tumor of head and neck
entities.anchor: Well-differentiated NETs have sparse site-specific driver data.
entities.pitfall: Includes laryngeal and middle-ear NETs; do not automatically assign the TP53/RB1 pattern of high-grade NEC.

entities.name: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of salivary gland
aliases: lacrimal adenoid cystic carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Adenoid cystic → MYB/MYBL1.
snv: Progression subset — NOTCH1 activation
rearr: Driver — MYB::NFIB; MYBL1::NFIB and alternative MYB/MYBL1 rearrangements
entities.pitfall: Includes salivary/lacrimal analogues; no fusion is universal.

entities.name: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Mucoepidermoid → CRTC1/3::MAML2.
rearr: Characteristic — CRTC1::MAML2 or CRTC3::MAML2
entities.pitfall: Fusion-negative cases occur, especially in high-grade differential diagnoses.

entities.name: Secretory carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Secretory → ETV6::NTRK3.
rearr: Characteristic — ETV6::NTRK3; alternative RET/MET-related fusions in small subsets
entities.pitfall: Same canonical fusion can appear in several distinct organs/lineages.

entities.name: Acinic cell carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Acinic → NR4A3 enhancer hijacking.
rearr: Characteristic — rearrangements activating NR4A3, often from SCPP-region enhancers
entities.pitfall: Regulatory rearrangement need not create a chimeric coding fusion.

entities.name: Polymorphous adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Polymorphous → PRKD1 E710D or PRKD fusions.
snv: Characteristic — PRKD1 E710D
rearr: Subset — PRKD1/2/3 rearrangements, enriched in cribriform-pattern tumors
entities.pitfall: Cribriform and conventional patterns grouped, while their molecular bias remains explicit.

entities.name: Hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Hyalinizing clear cell → EWSR1::ATF1.
rearr: Characteristic — EWSR1::ATF1; EWSR1::CREM alternatives
entities.pitfall: Distinct from melanoma-lineage clear cell sarcoma despite shared fusion partners.

entities.name: Salivary duct carcinoma
entities.anchor: Salivary duct → ERBB2 or RAS/PI3K subsets.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, HRAS, PIK3CA, PTEN
entities.pitfall: AR protein expression is common but is not itself an AR DNA alteration.

entities.name: Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma
entities.anchor: Biphasic salivary tumor → HRAS in a subset.
snv: Driver — HRAS, often codon 61
entities.pitfall: Absence of HRAS does not exclude the entity.

entities.name: Myoepithelial carcinoma of salivary gland
aliases: lacrimal myoepithelial carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Salivary myoepithelial carcinoma: PLAG1-associated subset.
rearr: Subset — PLAG1 or HMGA2 rearrangements, especially ex-pleomorphic-adenoma cases
entities.pitfall: Do not assume the EWSR1-fusion pattern of soft-tissue myoepithelial carcinoma.

entities.name: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
entities.anchor: A retained PLAG1/HMGA2 event can reveal the precursor.
snv: Progression — TP53 and other carcinoma-type alterations
rearr: Precursor-associated — PLAG1 or HMGA2 rearrangement
entities.pitfall: Carcinoma type determines additional drivers; the precursor rearrangement alone does not prove malignant transformation.

entities.name: Intraductal carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Intraductal salivary carcinoma can be RET-fusion driven.
snv: Apocrine subset — HRAS, PIK3CA
rearr: Subset — NCOA4::RET, TRIM27::RET and alternative kinase fusions
entities.pitfall: Most are indolent/intraductal; only malignant/invasive context is included, and fusion alone does not establish invasion.

entities.name: Microsecretory adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Microsecretory → MEF2C::SS18.
rearr: Characteristic — MEF2C::SS18
entities.pitfall: Distinct from SS18::SSX synovial sarcoma.

entities.name: Sclerosing microcystic adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: A rare salivary carcinoma without a reliable genetic hallmark.
entities.pitfall: Do not infer the genotype of cutaneous microcystic adnexal carcinoma from resemblance.

entities.name: Mucinous adenocarcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Salivary mucinous carcinoma → AKT1 E17K in subsets.
snv: Recurrent — AKT1 E17K
entities.pitfall: Papillary/colloid/signet-ring patterns grouped. Exclude metastasis.

entities.name: Basal cell adenocarcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Salivary basal cell malignancy has variable WNT biology.
snv: Subset — CTNNB1/CYLD-pathway alterations
entities.pitfall: A basal phenotype does not imply the PTCH1 pathway of skin BCC.

entities.name: Lymphoepithelial carcinoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: Salivary lymphoepithelial carcinoma may be EBV-driven.
other: Viral — EBV in a subset
entities.pitfall: EBV association is geographically variable; exclude a nasopharyngeal primary.

entities.name: Salivary carcinoma, NOS
entities.anchor: NOS is an exclusion category without a single driver.
entities.pitfall: Includes rare unclassified adenocarcinoma and carcinoma patterns; revisit molecularly defined entities first.

entities.name: Carcinosarcoma of salivary gland
entities.anchor: A biphasic salivary malignancy may arise from pleomorphic adenoma.
snv: Reported — TP53 alterations
rearr: Subset — PLAG1/HMGA2 precursor-associated rearrangements
entities.pitfall: No universal defining driver; small series limit inference.

entities.name: Ameloblastic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Ameloblastic carcinoma can retain MAPK activation.
snv: Subset — BRAF V600E
entities.pitfall: Molecular findings support but do not replace the odontogenic clinicopathologic diagnosis; rare-entity evidence is limited.

entities.name: Clear cell odontogenic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Clear-cell odontogenic → EWSR1 fusion.
rearr: Characteristic — EWSR1::ATF1 or EWSR1::CREB1
entities.pitfall: Molecular findings support but do not replace the odontogenic clinicopathologic diagnosis; rare-entity evidence is limited.

entities.name: Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Ghost-cell odontogenic → WNT.
snv: Subset — CTNNB1 activation
entities.pitfall: Molecular findings support but do not replace the odontogenic clinicopathologic diagnosis; rare-entity evidence is limited.

entities.name: Sclerosing odontogenic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Very rare; no established recurrent driver.
entities.pitfall: Molecular findings support but do not replace the odontogenic clinicopathologic diagnosis; rare-entity evidence is limited.

entities.name: Primary intraosseous carcinoma, NOS
entities.anchor: Intraosseous squamous carcinoma has no unique genetic signature.
entities.pitfall: Molecular findings support but do not replace the odontogenic clinicopathologic diagnosis; rare-entity evidence is limited.

entities.name: Endolymphatic sac tumor
entities.anchor: Endolymphatic sac tumor → VHL inactivation.
snv: Driver — VHL inactivation in a subset, including syndromic disease
entities.pitfall: Locally destructive tumor, rarely metastatic; included as a malignant-behavior site entity. VHL may be germline or somatic.

entities.name: Cutaneous melanoma
entities.anchor: Cutaneous melanoma → BRAF / RAS / NF1, with telomere and cell-cycle hits.
snv: Driver — BRAF, NRAS, NF1; KIT in selected acral/chronic-sun-damage contexts
Cooperating — TERT promoter, CDKN2A, PTEN
cnv: Subset — CDKN2A/PTEN loss; KIT/CCND1 gains in acral tumors
rearr: Spitz-lineage subset — ALK, ROS1, NTRK, RET, BRAF or MAP3K8 fusions
entities.pitfall: Superficial spreading, nodular, lentigo maligna, acral, desmoplastic, Spitz and nevus-associated pathways are nested; a broad genotype is not universal.

entities.name: Mucosal melanoma
entities.anchor: Mucosal melanoma → KIT/RAS/NF1 subsets and structural changes.
snv: Driver — KIT, NRAS, NF1; SF3B1 in selected sites
entities.pitfall: Head/neck, anorectal and genitourinary mucosal sites combined; BRAF V600 is less typical than in common cutaneous melanoma.

entities.name: Conjunctival melanoma
entities.anchor: Conjunctival melanoma resembles cutaneous more than uveal genetics.
snv: Driver — BRAF, NRAS, NF1
Cooperating — TERT promoter
entities.pitfall: Do not assume the GNAQ/GNA11 pattern of uveal melanoma.

entities.name: Primary meningeal melanoma
entities.anchor: Meningeal melanocytic tumors can use GNAQ/GNA11.
snv: Drivers — GNAQ, GNA11; NRAS in some diffuse/congenital-associated settings
entities.pitfall: Exclude metastatic melanoma and uveal primary; molecular findings depend on circumscribed versus diffuse disease.

entities.name: Basal cell carcinoma of skin
entities.anchor: BCC → Hedgehog pathway.
snv: Driver — PTCH1 loss or SMO activation; less often SUFU
Cooperating — TP53
entities.pitfall: Histologic variants and cutaneous sites combined; includes basosquamous phenotype.

entities.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of skin
entities.anchor: Cutaneous SCC → UV-associated tumor-suppressor loss.
snv: Drivers/cooperating — TP53, NOTCH1/2, CDKN2A; HRAS in subsets
other: Etiologic context — UV mutagenesis; HPV contributes in selected settings
entities.pitfall: Includes nail-unit and conjunctival squamous carcinomas as site analogues; invasive disease only.

entities.name: Merkel cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Merkel: viral T antigens or UV-driven TP53/RB1 loss.
snv: Virus-negative route — TP53 and RB1 inactivation
other: Viral route — Merkel cell polyomavirus integration and T-antigen expression
entities.pitfall: Two principal routes; absence of a high human mutation burden does not mean absence of an oncogenic driver.

entities.name: Sebaceous carcinoma
entities.anchor: Sebaceous: TP53/RB1 or mismatch-repair deficiency.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, RB1; MMR-gene inactivation in a subset
other: Subset — mismatch-repair deficiency, including Lynch/Muir–Torre context
entities.pitfall: Periocular and extraocular cases differ; an MMR-deficient tumor is not automatically germline disease.

entities.name: Porocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Porocarcinoma → YAP1 fusion in a subset.
snv: Cooperating — TP53, RB1, CDKN2A (subsets)
rearr: Driver — YAP1::NUTM1 or YAP1::MAML2
entities.pitfall: Fusion is also found in benign poroma; it does not itself prove carcinoma.

entities.name: Spiradenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Spiradenocarcinoma: ALPK1 or CYLD routes.
snv: Driver — ALPK1 V1092A or CYLD inactivation
Progression — TP53 in high-grade disease
entities.pitfall: These changes may already be present in benign precursors.

entities.name: Cylindrocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Malignant cylindroma can arise in CYLD-associated disease.
snv: Driver context — CYLD inactivation
entities.pitfall: Do not treat a germline CYLD variant or benign cylindroma as proof of malignancy.

entities.name: Hidradenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Hidradenocarcinoma may carry CRTC1::MAML2.
rearr: Subset — CRTC1::MAML2
entities.pitfall: Rare; the same fusion can occur in benign hidradenoma and other lineages.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous adenoid cystic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Cutaneous adenoid cystic → MYB-family activation.
rearr: Subset — MYB::NFIB / MYB rearrangement
entities.pitfall: Exclude metastasis or direct extension from a salivary primary.

entities.name: Secretory carcinoma of skin
entities.anchor: Cutaneous secretory → ETV6::NTRK3.
rearr: Characteristic — ETV6::NTRK3
entities.pitfall: Histologic context distinguishes this from other NTRK-fusion tumors.

entities.name: Myoepithelial carcinoma of skin
entities.anchor: Cutaneous myoepithelial carcinoma can be EWSR1-rearranged.
rearr: Subset — EWSR1 rearrangement with diverse partners
entities.pitfall: Genetics overlap soft-tissue myoepithelial tumors; not all cases have a fusion.

entities.name: Extramammary Paget disease, invasive
entities.anchor: Invasive Paget → ERBB2/RAS/PI3K subsets.
snv: Recurrent — ERBB2, PIK3CA, KRAS/NRAS (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Primary invasive disease included; epidermis-confined disease and secondary spread from an underlying carcinoma are distinguished.

entities.name: Pilomatrix carcinoma
entities.anchor: Pilomatrix lineage → CTNNB1.
snv: Driver — CTNNB1 activation
entities.pitfall: Also occurs in benign pilomatricoma; morphology establishes carcinoma.

entities.name: Trichilemmal carcinoma
entities.anchor: Rare follicular carcinoma without a fixed driver.
snv: Reported — TP53 and cell-cycle alterations
entities.pitfall: No validated universal mutation signature.

entities.name: Trichoblastic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Trichoblastic malignancy is not automatically PTCH1-driven BCC.
entities.pitfall: No established recurrent driver for a reliable memorization rule.

entities.name: Malignant proliferating pilar tumor
entities.anchor: Malignant pilar proliferation: cell-cycle abnormalities in small series.
snv: Reported — TP53 alterations
entities.pitfall: No defining genetic event; distinguish from cutaneous SCC.

entities.name: Malignant mixed tumor of skin
entities.anchor: Malignant chondroid syringoma can retain PLAG1 biology.
rearr: Reported — PLAG1 rearrangement in a subset
entities.pitfall: Fusion alone cannot distinguish benign from malignant mixed tumor.

entities.name: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma
entities.anchor: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma: no single validated driver.
entities.pitfall: Locally infiltrative skin carcinoma; do not infer salivary microsecretory MEF2C::SS18 biology.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous apocrine carcinoma
entities.anchor: Apocrine skin carcinoma: heterogeneous glandular-cancer pathways.
snv: Reported — PIK3CA, TP53
entities.pitfall: Exclude breast metastasis; AR/HER2 staining is not the same as a gene mutation or amplification.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous mucinous carcinoma
entities.anchor: Cutaneous mucinous carcinoma lacks a universal driver.
entities.pitfall: Exclude metastatic breast/GI carcinoma; no validated defining SNV/CNV/fusion.

entities.name: Digital papillary adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Digital papillary carcinoma: no routine defining human mutation.
entities.pitfall: Molecular evidence remains limited; do not assign an unproven universal fusion.

entities.name: Syringocystadenocarcinoma papilliferum
entities.anchor: A rare sweat-gland malignancy with limited genomic evidence.
snv: Reported — RAS/MAPK-pathway alterations in some precursor-associated cases
entities.pitfall: No established recurrent malignant-specific driver.

entities.name: Sweat gland carcinoma, NOS
entities.anchor: Adnexal carcinoma NOS is molecularly heterogeneous.
entities.pitfall: Includes otherwise unclassified eccrine/adnexal carcinoma; use named entities when criteria are met.

coverage.basis: Broad malignant tumor families based on public WHO structures and fifth-edition nomenclature; rare morphologic variants consolidated. Major molecular associations checked against primary studies and classification authors’ updates.
merged: Renal molecularly defined carcinomas remain separate because merging them would obscure defining drivers.
Testicular/ovarian/CNS germinoma-family tumors are one entry with site-specific caveats; other GCT lineages span sites.
Common glandular histotypes are separated where molecularly different; rare site variants are combined with aliases or explicit notes.
Skin melanoma pathways are nested inside one cutaneous melanoma entry; mucosal, conjunctival, uveal and meningeal disease are separately located.
Salivary counterparts cover lacrimal analogues without assuming identical prevalence.
Site-independent sarcomas and lymphomas are covered in their lineage sections; gynecologic ESS/adenosarcoma remain here.
excluded: Benign/borderline and in situ lesions, including clear cell papillary renal cell tumor, ovarian borderline tumors and mature ovarian teratoma.
Most benign testicular and ovarian stromal tumors; variable-behavior families are labelled malignant where applicable.
Metastatic involvement is not repeated as a new primary entity.
limitations: Not an exhaustive current-WHO code audit; selected exceptionally rare site-defined variants are consolidated.
Rare skin, genital and odontogenic carcinomas often lack adequate sequencing cohorts. Empty columns denote an evidence gap, not proven genetic absence.
Several rare-entity associations are based on small series; reported findings are not described as obligatory drivers.
Scope is a fifth-edition foundation and has not been fully reconciled against every sixth-edition volume.
